SearchAliases: person of the Way with no reliance

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Linji’s “person of the Way with no reliance” names the presently hearing person in his hall addresses, which call that person the mother of buddhas and the one who rides circumstances.
EvidenceBody: Literally, a person of the Way with no reliance . Linji repeatedly identifies this figure with the person presently listening to the teaching: 'the person of the Way with no reliance who is listening to the teaching right now' , plainly distinct and never lacking. He calls this person 'the mother of the buddhas' , says buddhas are born from no reliance, and says buddha-settings cannot name themselves—the person with no reliance rides the setting and comes out. He further says that although this person is the leaky substance of the five aggregates, it is earth-walking spiritual power, and that moving and not moving are two settings used by this person. The Zen bend is Linji's relocation of an apparently wandering ascetic title into the live teaching assembly: it names the hearer before him and the invariant person that uses changing named settings. Later records overwhelmingly quote, explain, challenge, and even warn against holding to this Linji formula; this distinct formulation therefore remains master-keyed.
